items.name: std.sql
items.description:
`std.sql`: the SQL sink. Like the prelude it is parsed in prelude mode and is signature-only; the runtime implementation comes with the interpreter (#9). A module sees these declarations only after `use std.sql`, as `sql.Db` and the like.

Query text is a **structural position**: it must be a `sql"..."` literal. Values enter a query only as parameters, a **data position**.

items.name: SqlLiteral
items.description: The text of a query. Only a `sql"..."` literal makes one: its field is private, so no other code can construct it.

items.name: Db
items.description: A database connection. It reaches the database over the network, so it is capability-bearing, and its field is private, so it can't be forged.

items.name: Db.query
items.signature: pub fn query(self, query: SqlLiteral, params: List<Untrusted<String>>) -> Result<List<Row>, SqlError>
items.description: Run `query`, binding each `?` in it to the next of `params`.

items.name: connect
items.signature: pub fn connect(net: NetConnect, url: String) -> Result<Db, SqlError>
items.description: Connect to the database at `url`. The URL decides where the program connects, so it is structural, like a `NetConnect` host.

items.name: Row
items.description: A result row. Its values come from the database, so they are untrusted.

items.name: Row.get
items.signature: pub fn get(self, column: String) -> Option<Untrusted<String>>

items.name: SqlError
items.signature: pub struct SqlError { pub message: Untrusted<String> }
